rationale.colonization: There is some expansion into peripheral relic regions and settlement, but no maritime colonization mainline.
rationale.complexity: Diplomacy, mage privileges, reforms, and magical thresholds stack together.
rationale.dark_story: Kidnapping, live research, and dehumanization become explicit late-game content.
rationale.difficulty: Several institutional and magical prerequisites are involved; this is not an in-game measurement.
rationale.diplomacy: Early relations with Sardan neighbours determine the opening route.
rationale.early_pressure: The country is easy to defend and lacks a safe direction of attack.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Blood magic, heart research, and the mage council are central.
rationale.narrative_density: Mitrenya, her partner, royal power, and research ethics create a distinctive story.
rationale.tall_play: Black soil, the capital, the mage estate, and research facilities need development.
rationale.trade_economy: Farmland and urban economies support the magical state-building project.
rationale.warfare: Opening the forest exit and expanding into Epednar regions gradually increases war demands.

identity.appearance: A three-province Sardan Ynnic feudal monarchy in 1444, ruled by Celadil I.
identity.formation_scope: Current G38 missions tell a story of magical expansion and institutional reorganization; a mandatory formation into the Ynnic Empire has not been verified.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas, and ambition only; racial and government bonuses and optional idea groups are excluded. Multiple candidates and conditions are listed separately and are not simultaneous additions; whether a formation accepts a new set depends on actual events, decisions, and player choice.

description.text: Detailing the grueling despair of the Sarda settlements that fell to the Epednar in the fourth and fifth centuries after Flood, the Book of Epadarkan is a somber reminder of what would happen to our people should we falter in front of barbarians.
description.text_en: Detailing the grueling despair of the Sarda settlements that fell to the Epednar in the fourth and fifth centuries after Flood, the Book of Epadarkan is a somber reminder of what would happen to our people should we falter in front of barbarians.

description.text: Vels Fadhecai, the Forest Beyond the River. A beautiful name, so beautiful it was copied from us three times over: not only by Vels Bacar upstream and Vels Domfan downstream, but even if we omit Vels there's Fadhevych on the other side of the Ynn… With little use arguing ours was the original name, this similarity has caused many letters and deliveries meant for Vels Fadhecai to arrive to one of the three other places, an unfortunate inconvenience which we have learned to deal with by always having a couple diplomats and canoe-couriers on standby.

description.text:
The black soil of the Fadhecan woodlands, known as "Tyerna Krarh", is perhaps the greatest blessing our fief received, allowing our peasants to produce plentiful food over small plots of land. This has allowed our towns to never suffer a famine, and thus their inhabitants could safely focus on crafts and trades, while peasants tilled the soil under the cover of the trees.

Vels Fadhecai's forest is the thickest of Sarda, providing a natural defense from the Epednar of the plains, but our crops can nonetheless withstand the darkness thanks to ancient magic. Because of this, we've never had to deforest the land, and our towns more often than not are sprawling on the sides of trees and hanging off of their branches, unless a war causes them to be destroyed, but, in those cases, many a town have been rebuilt more beautiful than before.

description.text:
Vels Fadhecai has always been the favourite location to exile dissidents to. Conspirators, disgraced knights, or just the occasional courtier who said the wrong thing at the wrong time. One such example of the latter was the poet Talvyr, who fell out of grace with Emperor Calrodiy I after jokingly calling him "the Battleking of the Ynnics".

Banished to Vels Fadhecai, Talvyr became an open dissident to Calrodiy's regime, writing poems that questioned the utility of war while in his verses he likened soldiers to brutes and knights to thugs. However, when a band of Epednar riders approached the town he was living in and he saw the local guards stand up for his protection, the seed of change was planted in Talvyr, and a year later he wrote his most famous book, "To the Garrisons".

Vels Fadhecai has seen many people arrive, from all walks of life and believing in radically different things. They all went through a similar story, a story where different people align together, and each contribute with their uniqueness, their individuality, in the face of a common threat.

description.text:
1581 marked the end of the regency for Lady Mitrenya, whose mother had died birthing her and whose father was assassinated while at a brothel. From the earliest age she showed great magical propensity, being able to conjure water bubbles and even water bombs she would hit her guardians with. When the War of the Bacaran succession erupted in 1602, Mitrenya was already a consummate war veteran, having led incursions into the Epednar territories over the past two decades, going as far as to reach the recently-founded city of Elathael during one of them.

It was thus to everyone's surprise when she announced she would maintain her neutrality during the Bacaran conflict.

Twenty years later, when the war was over, a shocking discovery was made: Mitrenya had been torturing the prisoners made during her past incursions, as well as some of her subjects and even relatives of her vassals. Not satisfied with water magic anymore, she would finish torturing them only to kill them then bathe in their blood; drawing power from it, using it to strengthen her magic and stay young forever.

With most of the Ynn still recovering from war, nobody moved to oppose Mitrenya, except for Vyr Arok yen Clovenvels, a mercenary captain of Escanni origin who ventured into the forests of Vels Fadhecai and defeated her many minions. Together with a small party of his most elite troops he snuck into Mitrenya's castle, where they slew her after a hard-fought battle.

description.text: It is an undeniable reality that many settlements have seen their rise and prosperity west of our fair woodlands over the recent decades. Their people have more in common with us than barbarians do, and, while it is sad to see them occupy what was our ancient homeland, acknowledging their success will be a necessary step to bring new life and prosperity to our lordship. Deals will have to be made, and an outer facade of friendship will need to be maintained, as we obtain new materials and techniques, and learn any secret deemed useful.

description.text:
"The first thing you need to understand, is that to defeat the barbarian, you must understand the barbarian. Think, smell, and ride like barbarians do. Secondly, always do what I tell you. You, with the weak frame and the slingshot. Come over here. If you survive training, I will make you a honorary half-orc."

-Address of a Chippengarder captain hired to train Fadhecan militias

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who want a straightforward conquest route or do not want human-experimentation material.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Manage the forest frontier, diplomacy, and mage privileges, then unlock magical reform and the Epednar route while negotiating the price of research.
player_overview.overview: In 1444, Vels Fadhecai begins with just three forest provinces, but defensible terrain and a tradition of magecraft. First secure neighbouring Sardan states, then follow Mitrenya's research and court conflicts as blood magic and the mage council become central to power. Its relationship story is nuanced and its magic develops strongly; later missions also explicitly depict secret kidnapping, experiments on hearts, and dehumanisation of outsiders. This is not a gentle story of liberation.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who like forest frontiers, character relationships, blood magic, and morally unreliable reformers.
signature_features: A closed forest frontier that must be opened through diplomacy and reform.
Mitrenya's relationship and the shift from royal rule to mage power.
Blood research and healing alongside explicit kidnapping and experimentation.
player_overview.tagline: A forest haven becomes a blood-magic power, and its liberation story exposes the cost paid by others.

reasons: Forest defence turns into Epednar expansion
Blood magic and research ethics are inseparable
warnings: The opening terrain and prerequisites slow expansion
The central story includes kidnapping and body experimentation

positive_indicators: Produces healing potions and magical knowledge
Organizes a new political role for mages
values.rationale: Refuge, agriculture, and medicine provide public benefits, but current mission text explicitly describes secret abductions, bodies used for heart research, and dehumanizing treatment of Epednar people. A milder reform does not automatically remove those harms.
red_flags: Using bodies and hearts as research material
